title: Temple of Athena Polias (Priene)
axis: Local +X follows the temple’s near east–west axis toward the altar. +Z is south toward the lower terrace.
source: OpenStreetMap identified temple ruins with Otto Bauer’s independent architectural survey
identityStatus: The independently named mapped outline places and orients the ruins. The 1965–66 German Archaeological Institute survey fixes stylobate sides to 37.233/37.167 m and 19.512/19.526 m. The survey plan is aligned to the midpoint of the approximately 38.8 by 14.0 m mapped extent.

terrainContact.basis: Unmodified public elevation at the center of the current temple ruins on the Athena terrace.

notes: The 2017 research and conservation account documents five standing columns on the north side, 7.92 m reconstructed column height, approximately 1.29 m lower diameter, 24 flutes and three stepped marble courses. The original CC0 photos show the present weathering, incomplete bases, inconsistent drum stacks, volutes and low masonry.
